correctness.rationale: For each family, box on an upper interval is controlled by the largest minimum of its members, diamond by their smallest maximum; the empty-family and empty-subset cases yield distinct sentinel pairs. All ordinary local pairs are realized by a single two-endpoint subset when b<=d or by two singletons when b>d. Modal operations are exactly the suffix minima of local thresholds; all nested formulas are preserved by induction. The unique empty-family prefix, terminal empty-subset case, and sole possible -1-to-positive diamond transition with an adjacent box equality give necessary and sufficient global normal forms. Stars-and-bars and the hockey-stick identity count these without overlap. A single top-world (n-1,0) pair proves the lower bound n>=2. Raw-small-frame exhaustive and randomized nested-modal checks corroborate all steps, with no finite-to-infinite inference.
